title: Elodie and the Protocol
premise: Tamsin Thackeray, the sole survivor of a crash that killed their family in row twelve, spends their career closing aviation cases governments prefer buried. When an anonymous voiceprint—matching their dead mother's voice—unlocks a server in Nairobi, they discover the crash was engineered by an international data-extraction protocol called ELARA, which is still active and still killing. Pursued by three governments who each want the evidence silenced for their own reasons, and hunted by the assassin who built the protocol's kill list, Tamsin must choose between loyalty to the mentor who protected them for years and the truth that will destroy him. They get the evidence airborne at dawn, but the cost is the mentor's confession broadcast to the world and the assassin's escape—leaving Tamsin alive, vindicated, and permanently unable to belong anywhere except the truth.
about_author: Beatrix Zhou is a former air-safety analyst who spent a decade writing incident reports no one read before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about the gap between what institutions know and what they admit.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Opening on the anniversary of the crash, Tamsin works a routine cargo incident in Reykjavik while flashbacks establish their family's deaths and their obsession with unattributed cases. Emotional beat: grief worn as professionalism, the wound that drives everything.

chapters.title: The Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A dead-letter file arrives containing a voiceprint that matches their mother—recorded three years after her death—unlocking a server in Nairobi. Tamsin runs the authentication twice, hands shaking. Emotional beat: vertigo, the impossible made procedural.

chapters.title: Cold Storage
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The server holds ELARA: flight manifests, insurance payouts, and a kill list with names Tamsin recognizes from closed cases. Among them, their own family. Emotional beat: the investigation becomes personal, rage replacing grief.

chapters.title: Mentor
chapters.summary: Tamsin visits Aldous Vane, their former supervisor, who taught them to close cases cleanly. He warns them off with unusual urgency. Tamsin notices his hands tremble. Emotional beat: loyalty tested at first contact; something is wrong beneath the kindness.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Within forty-eight hours, liaison officers from three governments contact Tamsin separately, each offering protection in exchange for the server's contents. Tamsin realizes everyone knows what they have. Emotional beat: the hunter realizes they've become the hunted.

chapters.title: Nairobi
chapters.summary: Tamsin flies to Nairobi against Vane's advice, following the server's physical origin to a shuttered data center. They find a technician, Amara Okonkwo, who uploaded the voiceprint deliberately. Emotional beat: first ally; the relief of not being alone.

chapters.title: Amara's Reasons
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara reveals her brother piloted one of the ELARA flights and was posthumously blamed. She chose Tamsin specifically because of row twelve. Emotional beat: two griefs recognizing each other; the alliance becomes a covenant.

chapters.title: The Kill List
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Decrypted files show the assassin—codename LATCH—has already been activated. Two names on the list are crossed off; both died in 'accidents' Tamsin once investigated. Emotional beat: horror of rereading their own career as a cover-up.

chapters.title: First Contact
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A near-miss in a hotel stairwell—LATCH is close, patient, testing their routines. Tamsin escapes through the kitchen with Amara's help. Emotional beat: fear made intimate; the assassin as a presence, not yet a face.

chapters.title: Vane's Call
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Vane calls, begging them to hand everything to him and disappear; he claims he can make it safe. Tamsin hears, for the first time, that Vane already knows too much about ELARA. Emotional beat: suspicion cracking the last loyalty.

chapters.title: The Protocol Explained
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara decodes ELARA's architecture: it doesn't cause crashes, it curates them—selecting flights whose losses serve financial and political interests, then laundering blame. Emotional beat: the scale of it; evil as spreadsheet, not spectacle.

chapters.title: Row Twelve, Revisited
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin finally opens the full file on their family's flight and learns their mother was a whistleblower whose voiceprint was harvested before her death. The 'voice' is bait—ELARA used her to draw Tamsin in. Emotional beat: devastation, then resolve; they were invited to this war.

chapters.title: London Interlude
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin meets the British liaison, Hargreaves, who seems honest—too honest—and reveals her government wants ELARA exposed but only the parts implicating rivals. Emotional beat: even allies have angles; trust becomes triage.

chapters.title: Safe House
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara and Tamsin hole up in a Mombasa safe house, copying the archive to physical media. Amara confesses she nearly took a payout to walk away. Emotional beat: vulnerability; loyalty chosen daily, not once.

chapters.title: LATCH Unmasked
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin identifies LATCH from a customs photo: a woman named Ilse Brandt, ex-military aviation security—someone Tamsin met once at a conference, who bought them coffee. Emotional beat: the assassin was kind to them; evil wears a familiar face.

chapters.title: The Betrayal Pattern
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Cross-referencing old cases, Tamsin finds every ELARA-adjacent investigation was closed by one supervisor: Vane. The pattern is undeniable. Emotional beat: grief for the mentor, arriving before the proof is even complete.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Hangar
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin confronts Vane at a maintenance hangar. He admits he closed the cases but claims he did it to protect Tamsin from the list—and that his name is on it too. Emotional beat: the truth is worse than treachery; it's cowardice wearing love.

chapters.title: Ilse's Offer
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse contacts Tamsin directly—not to kill them, but to recruit them: ELARA is fracturing, and she wants out with leverage. She offers the protocol's financial spine. Emotional beat: unsettling pragmatism; the assassin as a mirror of institutional logic.

chapters.title: Amara Taken
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The safe house is hit by a government extraction team, not Ilse. Amara is taken 'for questioning'; the archive copies are seized—or so it appears. Emotional beat: guilt and cold fury; Tamsin kept a decoy drive and hates themselves for it.

chapters.title: The Decoy Drive
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Interrogated in a Nairobi annex, Amara realizes the seized drive is the decoy and stalls her interrogators, feeding them false architecture. Emotional beat: courage under pressure; Amara becomes the story's quiet spine.

chapters.title: Hargreaves' Gambit
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Hargreaves offers to get Amara released if Tamsin gives Britain the real archive exclusively. Tamsin refuses—justice outside the law means no single flag owns the truth. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized; the refusal costs them their last institutional ally.

chapters.title: Vane's Confession, Part One
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane's chapters begin: he explains how, years ago, he was offered a choice between his career and the list, and chose the career—then spent a decade shielding Tamsin as penance. Emotional beat: a man dismantling himself in real time.

chapters.title: The Extraction Flight
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Ilse reveals the only way to move the archive past three governments: a dawn cargo flight out of Mombasa, chartered by a shell company ELARA itself uses. Using the enemy's route is the only door left. Emotional beat: desperate audacity; the clock starts.

chapters.title: Amara's Escape
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara exploits a transfer-window error to slip her handlers and reaches Tamsin by payphone, with a location and a warning: the annex knows about the flight. Emotional beat: reunion by voice only; hope with a timer on it.

chapters.title: Loading the Truth
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Night loading at the airfield—terabytes of evidence sealed in a crash-hardened case in the cargo hold. Vane appears uninvited, offering to fly as the named pilot so his credentials clear the manifest. Emotional beat: trust as a gamble; Tamsin lets him.

chapters.title: Ilse Changes Sides
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse burns her ELARA handler network to cover the flight's departure window, killing her own exit options. She tells Tamsin it's not redemption, it's arithmetic. Emotional beat: the assassin choosing, without sentiment, to be useful.

chapters.title: Hargreaves' Last Card
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Hargreaves threatens to flag the flight as a security risk, grounding it. Tamsin counters by leaking the archive's index to forty newsrooms simultaneously—if the plane goes down, the world will know what was aboard. Emotional beat: deterrence by daylight; the truth as armor.

chapters.title: Vane's Confession, Part Two
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. On the tarmac, Vane records a full confession naming every official who touched ELARA, to be released only if he dies. He hands Tamsin the dead man's switch. Emotional beat: penance completed; loyalty and truth finally pointing the same way.

chapters.title: Dawn
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The flight rolls at first light. Ground control tries to recall it; Vane answers with his credentials and a flat refusal. Two government jets shadow the climb. Emotional beat: terror and stillness; the whole book compressed into a climb-out.

chapters.title: Ilse's Last Stand
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse stays on the ground to delay the annex response team, buying the flight its corridor. She is wounded but vanishes into the city, status unknown. Emotional beat: the assassin's exit as an open question; sacrifice without absolution.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Mid-flight, a shadowing jet orders them down over international water. Vane, a decorated veteran, talks the intercept pilot down by naming the pilot's own father—another closed case, another ELARA flight. Emotional beat: the truth recruiting its own defenders midair.

chapters.title: Landing
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. They land at a neutral airfield under press watch, the dead man's switch armed, the archive mirrored in forty newsrooms. Officials arrive to negotiate rather than arrest. Emotional beat: the power inversion complete; the truth has leverage now.

chapters.title: The Reckoning
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Hearings begin. Vane's confession detonates across three governments; resignations cascade. Tamsin testifies not as a victim but as the investigator who was used. Emotional beat: justice outside the law forcing the law to catch up.

chapters.title: What Amara Kept
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara reveals she withheld one file: the identity of ELARA's architect—not Vane, but a committee, still partially intact. The fight isn't over. Emotional beat: sober hope; victory with loose threads.

chapters.title: Ilse, Alive
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A postcard arrives with no return address: a photo of row twelve's old seat map, and one word—'unfinished.' Ilse is alive, and watching. Emotional beat: unease braided with gratitude; the hunter who became something else.

chapters.title: Vane's Sentence
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane pleads guilty to obstruction and evidence tampering, refusing to bargain. In his final statement he names Tamsin as the only honest investigator he ever supervised. Emotional beat: forgiveness neither asked nor fully given; loyalty's last, hardest form.

chapters.title: Amara's Flight Home
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara returns to Nairobi to reopen her brother's case officially, her brother's name cleared in the first ELARA-related exoneration. She and Tamsin part at the gate as equals. Emotional beat: belonging found not in family but in witness; grief given a job.

chapters.title: Row Twelve, Closed
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin files the final report on their family's crash—their first case ever closed with the whole truth attached. At the graveside, they read the findings aloud. Emotional beat: catharsis; the wound acknowledged, not erased.

chapters.title: The Next Manifest
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. An envelope arrives: a new flight manifest with anomalies only Tamsin would notice, and a voiceprint—this time their own voice, saying 'you know what to do.' Tamsin packs a bag. Emotional beat: the loop reopens; the investigator who can no longer look away.

chapters.title: Dawn, Again
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Final chapter mirrors the first: Tamsin at an airfield at first light, no longer alone—Amara on comms, Ilse somewhere in the shadows, the truth as cargo. They board. Emotional beat: belonging redefined as purpose; the flight leaves at dawn, and this time they chose it.
